context.transcript_excerpt: Welcome to the Namibia Oil & Gas podcast, your weekly gateway to the latest news and developments shaping Namibia's dynamic oil and gas sector. It's Friday, 18 September 2026, and I'm Harrison Musimuko with the latest news, updates and insights from the Namibia oil and gas industry. Let's dive in. This week's top headlines. African Green Industries Summit places Africa's industrial future in focus. SDG Namibian One and Enersen signed founding agreement for Dauris' green fertilizer project. Nassan Energies completes first phase of service station rebranding program. Oratas Novi, oil and gas edition, to put youth perspective at the center of the national resource debate. Technip FMC expands its subsea engineering program. Namibia's oil and gas industry is growing and local businesses need to be ready for the opportunities ahead. The Namibia Local Content Conference and Exhibition 2026 will take place from 19th to 23rd October 2026 in Windhook under the theme Offshore Technology as a Pathway to Securing Namibia's Local Content Development. The conference brings together industry leaders, technology innovators, businesses and local content stakeholders to explore how offshore technology can drive local participation, build capacity and create opportunities for Namibian businesses. If you want to understand where Namibia's energy sector is heading, connect with key industry players and position your business for the future. This is the platform to be part of. Register now at www.nlcc.com.na slash registration dash form. Be in the room. Be part of the opportunity. Be part of Namibia's energy future. African Green Industries Summit places Africa's industrial future in focus. The inaugural African Green Industries Summit held in Swakopmund from 9 to 10 September to examine Africa's green industrialization ambitions. Held under the theme Powering African Industries for Sustainable Development the summit reflected a broader shift in Namibia green energy economy The summit reflected a broader shift in Namibia green economy agenda Discussions moved beyond green hydrogen alone to include renewable energy, critical materials, manufacturing, infrastructure, agriculture, and value addition. Organized by NEA Consulting under the patronage of the Government of Namibia and endorsed by the Ministry of Industries, Mines and Energy, the summit built on the platform previously created by the Global African Hydrogen Summit. A central message was that Africa's energy transition must be linked to industrial development, local value chains, skills creation and job opportunities. Namibia's green industrialization pipeline was presented as being worth approximately 20 billion US dollars while the government is seeking more than $1 billion in consensual finance to support project development. SDG Namibia One and Enocence signed funding agreement for Daores Green Fertilizer Project. SDG Namibia One has signed a development funding agreement with Enocence Energy Namibia to advance the Daores Green Fertilizer Project in Namibia's Irongo region. The project will use renewable energy and green hydrogen to produce low-carbon fertilizer for Namibian and regional markets, supporting agricultural productivity and food security while reducing reliance on imports. Nassen Energies completes first phase of service station rebranding program. Nassan Energies has completed the first phase in its service station rebranding program, making a significant step in the company's efforts to establish a strong and recognizable presence across Namibia. The first phase saw 16 former Shell service stations rebranded under the Nassan Energies name. The updated network includes locations in Ryoboth, Oshakati, Hobabes, Mariento, Kakval, Vintuk, Okahanja, Okahao, Volfish Bay, Tumeb, Ondangwa, and Oshivelo, among other areas.
